title: Main Landing Gear Bay Harness Re-Routing and Terminal Block Relocation Clear of the Door Actuator

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

ata.title: Centre Fuselage Wiring — Landing Gear Bay Wiring

abstract: Re-routing of the main gear bay harness and relocation of its terminal block, after repeated insulation damage was found where the harness crossed the sweep of the gear door actuator.

sections.reason: Insulation damage in the main landing gear bay harness was reported thirty-eight times between 2019 and 2021, always on the same section and always on aircraft operating from stations where the gear bay collects debris and standing water. Investigation showed that the harness ran within twenty millimetres of the gear door actuator sweep and that the clearance was consumed whenever the harness was re-clipped after a component change. Two of the events resulted in a gear door position indication fault in flight, and one resulted in an unscheduled gear swing on the ground to clear the fault.
sections.description: The harness is re-routed forty millimetres outboard along the bay roof, clear of the actuator sweep in all door positions, and the contactor BED352373-29 is moved with it. The terminal block at FIN 1396VC is relocated to a new bracket on the bay side wall, and the bus bar at FIN 622VC7 is re-terminated at the new position, which shortens the run by a third of a metre. Cable ties AGS700897-7A of the correct section are specified because a proportion of the reported damage was caused by over-tightened ties of the wrong size. Work is in zones 145, 572 and 721 with the gear down and locked, the ground locks fitted and the gear doors held open. The revised route and the new bracket positions are on drawing D92311222260.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 1.1 kilograms per aircraft. No electrical load change; the shorter run reduces voltage drop marginally on the door position circuit. Not interchangeable, because the side wall bracket is drilled at embodiment. The harness clearance inspection in the gear bay changes from a detailed inspection to a general visual and the clearance figure is published on the wiring sheet. The wiring sheet, the gear bay zonal inspection and the parts data all require re-issue.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN Z11011 in September 2022. Retrofit is by service bulletin during a base maintenance visit with the gear bay open; sixteen hours per aircraft is quoted, most of it re-termination. Kits contain the bracket, the tie set and the revised harness support hardware.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z11011 with the bay harness build standard changed together
